reading.text:
Unit: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Martingale.naturalFiltration (reading locked before any Lean is seen)

Paper notion. Section 2, line 228: "(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the one generated by W, N and an
independent initial sigma-field F_0". The raw filtration generated by a process X is the natural
filtration F^X_t = sigma(X_s : 0 <= s <= t). This unit is (presumably) the natural filtration of a
real (scalar) process, used as an ingredient of the generated/augmented filtration.

What a faithful Lean definition must be.
- For a process X : time -> Omega -> R (each X_s measurable for the ambient sigma-algebra):
  F_t = the sigma-algebra generated by {X_s : s <= t} (supremum over s <= t of comap X_s of the Borel
  sigma-algebra), as a Mathlib Filtration (monotone, each <= the ambient sigma-algebra).
- Time index: [0,oo) (R_{>=0}) or [0,T]; if the index is R, times s < 0 must not add information not
  in the paper (if the process is only meaningful for s >= 0, including s < 0 values is harmless only
  if those values are determined, e.g. by a convention).
- No null sets and no right-continuity: those belong to the augmentation (a separate unit).
- The inequality "<= ambient" requires measurability of each X_s; if the Lean definition needs that as
  a hypothesis it should take it; a junk value (e.g. bottom or the ambient) when measurability fails is
  harmless only for measurable processes, which is the paper's case.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Martingale.naturalFiltration
(Brownian/Martingale.lean:65-70; Mathlib Filtration.natural: seq t = sup_{j <= t} comap (W j) Borel.)

- Reading: F_t = sigma(X_s : s <= t), a Mathlib Filtration, raw (no null sets, no right-continuity),
  each <= ambient (measurable values).
- Lean: Filtration.natural W.W (each W.W t strongly measurable from BrownianMotion.measurable_eval), i.e.
  F_t = sup_{j <= t} comap (W_j) Borel. Exactly the natural filtration of a (1-dim) BrownianMotion. Raw.
- Time index R: j ranges over all reals <= t, including j < 0. BrownianMotion has W_j = 0 a.s. for j < 0
  (negative_zero), so the sigma-algebras comap W_j, j < 0, consist of events of probability 0 or 1; they
  add only P-trivial events, which are independent of everything and disappear in the augmentation the
  paper applies.
- It is the natural filtration of a BrownianMotion specifically (not of an arbitrary process), which is
  the role it plays (component of the generated filtration of W).

Verdict: faithful with representation choices (R-indexed time; negative-time values add only P-trivial
events).

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. Time is R rather than [0,oo): F_t = sup over all j <= t, including j < 0, of sigma(W_j). By the
   BrownianMotion convention W_j = 0 a.s. for j < 0, those sigma-algebras contain only events of probability
   0 or 1, so the filtration differs from sigma(W_s : 0 <= s <= t) only by P-trivial events: independence
   statements are unaffected and the difference is absorbed by the null-set augmentation that the paper's
   standing filtration applies. For t < 0 the filtration is P-trivial, and the paper has no negative times.
2. It is defined for a BrownianMotion (the only process the paper takes a natural filtration of, besides N,
   which has its own definition).
